_schema.status: verified = read from a cited source; method = a modelling choice, documented here; example = a stand-in shown as such in the app

tyre_longitudinal.model: Magic Formula, pure longitudinal slip (Sharp, Evangelou & Limebeer 2004, eqs. 1–6)
tyre_longitudinal.tyre: 160/70 ZR17 sport radial, fitted to test data reproduced by Pacejka
tyre_longitudinal.note: Table I. Used for both wheels and scaled to the surface by μ ÷ 1.2017; it is not a fit to the Royal Enfield tyres, for which no data is published.

wheel_spin_inertia_kgm2.note: Table A.II (Ifwy, Irwy), measured on a Suzuki GSX-R1000; used as stand-ins because Royal Enfield publishes no inertias.

pitch_inertia_kgm2.note: Table A.II: Imny (main frame, including the rider's lower body) and Iubry (rider's upper body), GSX-R1000; used as stand-ins about each body's own centre of gravity.

brake_capacity.note: Full lever gives 1.3 × 1.2 × (the most load the wheel can carry with the rider alone) × wheel radius: enough to lock either wheel on dry asphalt. Fixed for the motorcycle, so a pillion or luggage does not change it. Royal Enfield publishes no brake torques.

abs.note: A generic slip-band controller around the tyre model's own peak slip, not a manufacturer's algorithm.

unsprung_mass_kg.note: Table A.I: front wheel 11.9 + front suspension parts 7.25; rear wheel 14.7 + swing arm 8.0 (GSX-R1000), used as stand-ins.

tyre_radial_stiffness_N_per_m.note: Table A.V (fkt, rkt), sport tyres, used as stand-ins.

rider_sag.note: About 30 % of the travel used with rider (and luggage) aboard; the example value when your own sag is not entered.

suspension_model.note: Linear springs without preload, rates set so that the rider-aboard sag is as entered; damping as a fraction of critical, the same in compression and rebound (no published damping data for these bikes); stiff end stops at full extension and full compression.

powertrain.note: Stand-ins: 90 % from crankshaft to rear tyre; 0.15 s without drive during a shift; rev limit 1000 rpm above peak power; torque at idle 65 % of the peak. The torque curve passes exactly through the published peak torque and peak power; its shape elsewhere is an assumption.

road_load.note: Air at 15 °C at sea level; rolling-resistance coefficient a stand-in. The drag area CdA of each bike with its rider is back-solved from its reported top speed, where the power at the rear wheel equals drag plus rolling resistance.

lateral_model.note: Stand-ins measured on a Suzuki GSX-R1000 and its rider (Sharp et al. 2004, Tables A.I–A.III), because Royal Enfield publishes no part masses or inertias. Wheels: Mfw, Mrw, Ifwx, Irwx. Front frame: the steered upper part (9.99 kg, Iff_str) plus the lower fork (7.25 kg) as a point mass, combined about their joint centre of mass, which lies on the steering axis 0.30 m above the front axle; inertias along and across the fork. Main frame (Imn, which includes the rider's lower body) for the motorcycle, and the rider's upper body (Iubr) for each rider and pillion. Products of inertia are tensor elements (Hx = Ixx·ωx + Ixz·ωz, z down), as in Meijaard et al. 2007.

rider_steering.note: The rider steers by handlebar torque from the lean-angle error and the lean rate, the controller form of Sharp et al. 2004 (section 6), with the torque the steady turn needs fed forward in place of their integral term. The gains give the closed loop a double root at −3.89 ÷ (the roll-in time), so that a step in the wanted lean is 90 % complete in about that time. The rider's arms deliver the torque through a first-order lag of 0.1 s, the neuromuscular delay for steering torque that Åström et al. 2005 report from a study of motorcyclists.
